faqs.q: In which year was the Special Police Establishment set up by the Government of India?
The Special Police Establishment was originally set up to investigate cases of bribery and corruption in transactions with which department during World War II?
Which Act transferred the superintendence of the Special Police Establishment to the Home Department and enlarged its functions to cover all departments of the Government of India?
In which year was the CBI established by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs?
faqs.e: The Delhi Special Police Establishment was merged with the CBI and made one of its divisions; the CBI was later transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

faqs.q: The CBI derives its powers from which Act, since it is not a statutory body?
The CBI functions under the administrative control of which Ministry?
faqs.e: Specifically, the CBI functions under the administrative control of the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) of the Ministry of Personnel.

faqs.q: The National Investigation Agency was constituted mainly for investigating terror-related crimes following which incident, distinguishing its role from that of the CBI?
faqs.e: The CBI, in contrast, investigates crime of corruption, economic offences and serious organised crime other than terrorism.

faqs.q: Under the provisions of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, the CBI's jurisdiction can be extended to a state (not being a railway area) only with:

options.a: the approval of the Central Vigilance Commission
options.b: the permission of the Supreme Court
options.c: the consent of the State Government concerned

faqs.a: the consent of the State Government concerned

faqs.q: What is the motto of the CBI?
Who heads the CBI?
faqs.e: The Director of CBI functions as Inspector-General of Police, Delhi Special Police Establishment, and is responsible for the administration of the organisation.

faqs.q: With the enactment of the CVC Act, 2003, the superintendence of the Delhi Special Police Establishment vests with the Central Government, except for investigations under which Act, where superintendence vests with the Central Vigilance Commission?

Which Act amended the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 to introduce changes in the composition of the CBI, including provisions for the appointment of the Director of CBI and the Director of Prosecution?

As per the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Director of CBI is appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a three-member committee. Which of the following statements about this committee is/are correct?
(I) The Prime Minister is the Chairperson.
(II) The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member.
(III) The Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court nominated by him/her is a member.
Which of the above is/are correct?

The Delhi Special Police Establishment (Amendment) Act, 2014 provided that where there is no recognized Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, who would be a member of the committee for appointment of the Director of CBI instead?

options.a: Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
options.c: Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.d: Leader of the single largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha

faqs.a: Leader of the single largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha

faqs.q: Under the CVC Act, 2003, what was the originally fixed tenure of the Director of CBI?
faqs.e: The Delhi Special Police Establishment (Amendment) Act, 2021 allowed the Central Government to extend this tenure up to five years in total, through annual extensions of up to one year each, not exceeding three such extensions.

faqs.q: As per the Delhi Special Police Establishment (Amendment) Act, 2021, what is the maximum total tenure (including the initial appointment) that the Director of CBI can serve through extensions?
faqs.e: Extensions can be granted up to one year at a time, in public interest, on the recommendation of the appointing Committee, with reasons recorded in writing.

faqs.q: The CBI is required to obtain prior approval of the Central Government before investigating an offence committed by officers of which rank and above?

In 2014, the Supreme Court held Section 6A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act — which made prior sanction mandatory for CBI probes against senior bureaucrats in corruption cases — as violative of which Article of the Constitution?
The Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE), a division of the CBI, enjoys concurrent powers of investigation and prosecution with the state police forces for offences under which Act?
The CBI acts as which of the following in India?
The institution of Ombudsman was first created in which country?
faqs.e: The institution of Ombudsman was first created in Sweden in 1809; 'Ombud' is a Swedish term referring to a person who acts as a representative or spokesman of another.

faqs.q: Which country is credited with adopting the Ombudsman system as the first Commonwealth country to do so, in the form of a Parliamentary Commissioner for Investigation?
faqs.e: New Zealand adopted this in 1962; the United Kingdom adopted a similar institution called the Parliamentary Commissioner for Administration in 1967.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Swedish Ombudsman:
(I) It deals with maladministration and administrative corruption.
(II) It has no power to reverse or quash an administrative decision.
(III) Its jurisdiction excludes the judiciary.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Unlike New Zealand's Lokpal-Lokayukta model, in Sweden the judiciary is within the purview of the Ombudsman.

faqs.q: Which institutional device for redressal of citizens' grievances, created in the socialist countries like the former USSR and China, is referred to as the 'Procurator System'?
faqs.e: The French system of Administrative Courts is another distinct institutional device, which spread to other countries due to its success in France.

faqs.q: Which Commission of India first recommended the setting up of the institutions of 'Lokpal' and 'lokayukta'?
faqs.e: The First ARC (1966–1970) recommended these institutions on the pattern of the Ombudsman in Scandinavian countries and the parliamentary commissioner for investigation in New Zealand.

faqs.q: As per the recommendation of the First Administrative Reforms Commission, the Lokpal would deal with complaints against which of the following?

options.c: Ministers and Secretaries at Central and state levels

faqs.a: Ministers and Secretaries at Central and state levels
faqs.e: The lokayukta (one at the Centre and one in every state) would deal with complaints against other specified higher officials; the ARC kept the judiciary outside the purview of Lokpal and lokayukta.

faqs.q: As per the First ARC's recommendation, who would appoint the Lokpal?

options.d: President, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Speaker of Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

faqs.a: President, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Speaker of Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

faqs.q: The tenth official attempt at Lokpal legislation, introduced as the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011, was enacted as the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act in which year?
Which government first introduced a Lokpal Bill in the Parliament, in May 1968?

options.a: NDA Government headed by A.B. Vajpayee
options.b: Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai
options.c: Congress Government headed by Indira Gandhi
options.d: National Front Government headed by V.P. Singh

faqs.a: Congress Government headed by Indira Gandhi

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013:
(I) The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson with a maximum of 8 members.
(II) At least 50% of the members shall be judicial members.
(III) At least 50% of the members shall come from amongst the SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women.
Which of the above is/are correct?

Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Selection Committee for choosing the Chairperson and members of the Lokpal consists of the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the Chief Justice of India (or a nominated Supreme Court Judge), and which other member?

options.b: An eminent jurist nominated by the President

faqs.a: An eminent jurist nominated by the President
faqs.e: This eminent jurist is nominated by the President on the basis of recommendations of the first four members of the Selection Committee. A Search Committee, with 50% membership from SCs/STs/OBCs/minorities/women, assists the Selection Committee.

faqs.q: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, who chairs the High-Powered Committee that recommends the selection of the Director of CBI?
As per the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, what is the maximum punishment prescribed under the Prevention of Corruption Act after enhancement by this Act?
faqs.e: The Act enhanced the maximum punishment from seven years to ten years, and raised the minimum punishment under sections 7, 8, 9 and 12 to three years.

faqs.q: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, entities receiving foreign contributions in excess of how much per year, under the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA), are brought under the jurisdiction of the Lokpal?
The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 mandates that states enact a law setting up the institution of Lokayukta within how many days from the commencement of the Act?
Which of the following is a drawback of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?

options.a: Lokpal has no power over the CBI
options.b: Lokpal cannot investigate Group A officers
options.c: Lokpal cannot receive complaints against Ministers
options.d: Lokpal cannot proceed suo motu against any public servant

faqs.a: Lokpal cannot proceed suo motu against any public servant
faqs.e: Other drawbacks include disallowing anonymous complaints, a 7-year limitation period for filing complaints, and a non-transparent procedure for complaints against the PM.

faqs.q: What is the limitation period prescribed for filing complaints to the Lokpal under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?
The institution of lokayukta was established first in which state, even though another state had passed the relevant Act earlier?
faqs.e: Maharashtra established its lokayukta in 1971, though Odisha had passed the enabling Act in 1970.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the institution of lokayukta in Indian states:
(I) The lokayukta and upalokayukta are appointed by the Governor of the state.
(II) The term of office for lokayukta is uniformly fixed at 5 years across all states.
(III) The recommendations made by the lokayukta are only advisory and not binding on the state government.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: While the term of office in most states is 5 years or 65 years of age (whichever is earlier), this is not uniform across all states, so statement (II) is incorrect.

faqs.q: To whom does the lokayukta present its annual consolidated performance report?

options.a: Chief Justice of the High Court

faqs.e: The Governor places this report, along with an explanatory memorandum, before the state legislature.

faqs.q: In which year was the National Investigation Agency constituted under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008?
The NIA was established in the backdrop of which incident?
Where is the headquarters of the NIA located?
The NIA has a specialised cell dealing with fake currency notes and terror funding, known as:
Who heads the NIA?
faqs.e: The Director-General's powers are similar to those exercisable by a Director-General of Police in respect of the police force in a state; he/she is appointed by the Central Government.

faqs.q: The NIA works under the administrative control of which Ministry?
Which Commission's recommendations, along with several expert committees, contributed to the rationale for establishing the NIA?
In which year was the jurisdiction of the NIA extended to cover offences relating to human trafficking, counterfeit currency, prohibited arms, cyber-terrorism, and explosive substances?
faqs.e: This extension was made through the NIA (Amendment) Act, 2019.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the NIA (Amendment) Act, 2019:
(I) It applied the provisions of the NIA Act to persons committing a scheduled offence outside India against Indian citizens or India's interests.
(II) It empowered NIA officers to exercise powers similar to police officers not only in India but also outside India.
(III) It allowed the central and state governments to designate Sessions Courts as Special Courts for trial of NIA Act offences.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Under which offence category is the NIA empowered to investigate attacks on nuclear installations and use of weapons of mass destruction?

options.d: Terror attacks under its concurrent jurisdiction

faqs.a: Terror attacks under its concurrent jurisdiction

faqs.q: Following which disaster did the Government of India enact the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
faqs.e: A High Powered Committee had been set up in 1999 and a National Committee in 2001 (after the Gujarat earthquake) even before the Act was enacted.

faqs.q: The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) was initially constituted in 2005 by an Executive Order, and was later notified under the provisions of the Disaster Management Act, 2005 in which year?
Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of the NDMA?
What is the maximum number of members (excluding the chairperson) that the NDMA can have?
faqs.e: The other members are nominated by the chairperson; one of them is designated as vice-chairperson, who holds the status of a Cabinet Minister, while the remaining members hold the status of a Minister of State.

faqs.q: The NDMA works under the administrative control of which Ministry?
The NDMA exercises general superintendence, direction and control over which specialist response force?
Which body lays down broad policies and guidelines for the functioning of the National Institute of Disaster Management?
faqs.e: The National Institute of Disaster Management is located in New Delhi.

faqs.q: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, who is the ex-officio chairperson of the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)?
faqs.e: The chairperson of the State Executive Committee is an ex-officio member of the SDMA and also acts as its ex-officio chief executive officer.

faqs.q: What is the maximum number of members (excluding the chairperson) that an SDMA can have?
Who is the ex-officio chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)?

options.b: Collector (District Magistrate/Deputy Commissioner) of the district
options.c: Chief Executive Officer of the DDMA
options.d: Superintendent of Police of the district

faqs.a: Collector (District Magistrate/Deputy Commissioner) of the district

faqs.q: In the case of Tribal Areas under the Sixth Schedule to the Constitution of India, who acts as the ex-officio co-chairperson of the DDMA instead of the elected representative of the local authority?

options.d: Chief executive member of the district council of the autonomous district

faqs.a: Chief executive member of the district council of the autonomous district

faqs.q: What is the maximum number of members (excluding the chairperson) that a DDMA can have?

Consider the following statements regarding the DDMA:
(I) The DDMA acts as the district planning, coordinating and implementing body for disaster management.
(II) It follows guidelines laid down by the NDMA and the SDMA.
(III) Its chief executive officer is appointed by the NDMA.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: The chief executive officer of the DDMA is appointed by the state government, not the NDMA.

faqs.q: The Bar Council of India (BCI) was established under which legislation?
faqs.e: Being established by an Act of Parliament, the BCI is a statutory, not a constitutional, body.

faqs.q: Who chaired the All India Bar Committee appointed in 1951 by the Government of India to examine the reorganisation of the Bar and legal profession?
Which body's 1958 report again endorsed the All India Bar Committee's recommendation to establish an All India Bar Council and State Bar Councils, leading to the passage of the Advocates Act, 1961?

options.a: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution

faqs.q: The BCI works under the Department of Legal Affairs of which Ministry?

options.c: Union Ministry of Law and Justice
options.d: Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

faqs.a: Union Ministry of Law and Justice

faqs.q: Which of the following are ex-officio members of the Bar Council of India?

options.a: Solicitor-General of India and Law Secretary
options.b: Chief Justice of India and Attorney-General of India
options.c: Law Secretary and Attorney-General of India
options.d: Attorney-General of India and Solicitor-General of India

faqs.a: Attorney-General of India and Solicitor-General of India

faqs.q: For how long do the Chairman and Vice-Chairman of the BCI, elected by the Council from amongst its members, hold office?
Which of the following is NOT one of the standing committees of the BCI?
faqs.e: The Enrolment Committee is a committee of the State Bar Councils, not the BCI; the BCI has a Legal Education Committee instead.

faqs.q: Which function is exclusively performed by the BCI and not by a State Bar Council?

options.a: To entertain cases of misconduct against advocates on its roll
options.b: To admit persons as advocates on its roll
options.c: To promote the growth of Bar Associations
options.d: To recognise foreign law qualifications on a reciprocal basis for enrolment as an advocate

faqs.a: To recognise foreign law qualifications on a reciprocal basis for enrolment as an advocate

faqs.q: The Advocates Act, 1961 provides for the establishment of a State Bar Council (SBC) for each state, or a common SBC for:

options.b: group of states with more than 10,000 advocates
options.c: two or more states, or for a state and a union territory
options.d: only a state and its neighbouring union territory

faqs.a: two or more states, or for a state and a union territory

faqs.q: At present, how many State Bar Councils (SBCs) are there in India?
In the case of a State Bar Council with an electorate of more than ten thousand advocates, how many elected members does it have?
faqs.e: A SBC with an electorate of five thousand has 15 members, one with five to ten thousand has 20 members, and one with more than ten thousand has 25 members; one-half of the elected members must have been advocates on a state roll for ten years.

faqs.q: What is the term of office of an elected member of a State Bar Council?
faqs.e: If the SBC fails to hold elections before the term expires, the BCI may extend this term by a period of six months.

faqs.q: In the case of the State Bar Council of Delhi, who serves as the ex-officio member, distinct from the Advocate-General role in other SBCs?
The Advocates Act, 1961 provides for two categories of advocates entitled to practise law before the Courts, namely:
Which body deals with the designation of Advocates as Senior Advocates in the Supreme Court, under the Supreme Court Rules, 2013?

options.d: Chief Justice of India and the Judges

faqs.a: Chief Justice of India and the Judges
faqs.e: A Permanent Committee constituted by the CJI deals with all matters relating to this designation, comprising the CJI as Chairperson, the two seniormost Supreme Court Judges, the Attorney-General for India, and a nominated member of the Bar.

faqs.q: A Senior Advocate is not entitled to appear in the Supreme Court without which of the following?

options.c: A written brief from the Bar Council
options.d: A no-objection certificate from the SBC

faqs.q: In which year did the system of "Agents" in the Supreme Court get substantially modified and replaced by "Advocates-on-Record"?
faqs.e: When introduced in 1954, an Advocate of seven years standing was entitled to get registered as an Advocate-on-Record if he/she fulfilled the prescribed conditions; the Advocate-on-Record examination itself was introduced later, in 1959.

faqs.q: In which year were the Supreme Court Rules amended to introduce the Advocate-on-Record examination?
"Other Advocates" — those whose names are entered on the roll of a State Bar Council — cannot appear, plead or address the Supreme Court on behalf of a party unless:

options.a: instructed by an Advocate-on-Record or permitted by the Court
options.b: they hold a Senior Advocate designation
options.c: they have practised for at least ten years
options.d: they are members of the Bar Council of India

faqs.a: instructed by an Advocate-on-Record or permitted by the Court

faqs.q:
Consider the following states/UTs and their corresponding State Bar Councils:
(I) Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa – Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
(II) Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana – Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh
(III) Bar Council of West Bengal – West Bengal and Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: There are 24 State Bar Councils in total, some covering multiple states/UTs jointly, such as the Bar Council of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Mizoram and Nagaland, and the Bar Council of Kerala (covering Kerala and Lakshadweep).

faqs.q: The Law Commission of India is best described as:
faqs.e: It is established by an order of the Central Government from time to time for a fixed tenure, and its recommendations are not binding on the government.

faqs.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides that pre-Constitution laws shall remain in force until amended or repealed, providing part of the rationale for establishing a Law Commission after Independence?
Who headed the First Law Commission of independent India, established in 1955?
faqs.e: M.C. Setalvad was the then Attorney-General of India; the term of this Commission was three years.

faqs.q: What is the standard tenure of each Law Commission of India constituted since 1955?
Which pre-independence Law Commission was chaired by Lord Macaulay?
faqs.e: See table below for the details of all four pre-independence Law Commissions.

faqs.q: Which of the following laws was NOT among the products of the four pre-independence Law Commissions?
faqs.e: The four pre-independence Commissions produced the Indian Penal Code, Criminal Procedure Code, Civil Procedure Code, Indian Contract Act, Indian Evidence Act, Transfer of Property Act, and other laws; the Advocates Act was enacted much later, in 1961.

faqs.q: Who chaired the 22nd Law Commission of India, whose chairman and members were appointed nearly two and a half years after its constitution?
faqs.e: The 22nd Law Commission was constituted on 21st February, 2020, for a three-year term; its term was later extended up to 31st August, 2024.

faqs.q: In the composition of a Law Commission, the Member-Secretary belongs to which service and holds the rank of Additional Secretary or Secretary to the Government of India?
Which of the following is a function of the Law Commission of India?

options.a: To conduct elections to local bodies
options.b: To appoint judges of the High Courts
options.c: To draft the annual Union Budget
options.d: To identify laws which are no longer needed or relevant and can be repealed

faqs.a: To identify laws which are no longer needed or relevant and can be repealed

faqs.q: The reports of the Law Commission are considered and submitted to Parliament through which Ministry?
The high-powered body responsible for fixing limits/boundaries of territorial constituencies is known as the Delimitation Commission or:
The Delimitation Commission of India is best described as:
faqs.e: It is established by the Central Government under a law enacted by Parliament, to demarcate boundaries of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies.

faqs.q: Orders of the Delimitation Commission come into force on a date specified by whom?
faqs.e: These orders have the force of law, cannot be challenged in any court, and modifications are not permissible even when laid before the Lok Sabha and the concerned State Legislative Assembly.

faqs.q: Under which Act was the First Delimitation Commission of India established, in 1952?

options.a: The Representation of the People Act, 1950

faqs.q:
Consider the following Delimitation Commissions and the Acts under which they were established:
(I) Second Delimitation Commission (1963) – The Delimitation Commission Act, 1962
(II) Third Delimitation Commission (1973) – The Delimitation Act, 1972
(III) Fourth Delimitation Commission (2002) – The Delimitation Act, 2002
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
Which set of Articles of the Constitution deal with the delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies?
Which Constitutional Amendment Act, along with the 87th Amendment Act of 2003, amended Articles 81, 82, 170, 330 and 332 relating to delimitation?
As per the 84th and 87th Constitutional Amendment Acts, the total number of existing Lok Sabha seats allocated to states shall remain unaltered until the first census taken after which year?
faqs.e: This freeze also applies to the total number of existing seats in state Legislative Assemblies; however, seats reserved for SCs/STs were re-worked on the basis of the 2001 census.

faqs.q: On the basis of which census were states re-delimited into territorial parliamentary and assembly constituencies under the 84th and 87th Amendments?
Who was appointed as the Chairperson of the Fourth Delimitation Commission of 2002?
In which year did the President of India sign the notification implementing the recommendations of the Fourth Delimitation Commission, redefining Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies?
faqs.e: The Commission had submitted its recommendations to the Government in 2007.

faqs.q: The recommendations of the Fourth Delimitation Commission were not made applicable to which of the following states, whose delimitation exercise was deferred or nullified?

options.a: Assam, Bihar, Odisha, Kerala and Punjab
options.b: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Assam and Tripura
options.c: Sikkim, Tripura, Mizoram, Meghalaya and Goa
options.d: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Nagaland and Jharkhand

faqs.a: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Nagaland and Jharkhand
faqs.e: The delimitation exercise was deferred in the four north-eastern states, while the Commission's final order for Jharkhand was nullified.

faqs.q: In which month and year did the Government of India rescind its earlier notifications deferring delimitation in the four north-eastern states (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Nagaland)?
Who was appointed as the Chairperson of the Delimitation Commission set up in March 2020 for the north-eastern states and the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir?
In March 2021, the Government of India removed which states from the purview of the 2020 Delimitation Commission, leaving it to focus on the UT of Jammu and Kashmir?
In which month and year did the 2020 Delimitation Commission complete its task relating to the delimitation of the UT of Jammu and Kashmir?
Under the delimitation order for the UT of Jammu and Kashmir, how many Assembly constituencies were created in total, treating J&K as a single entity for delimitation?
faqs.e: Of these, 43 are in the Jammu region and 47 are in the Kashmir region; all 5 Parliamentary constituencies now have an equal number of 18 Assembly constituencies each.

faqs.q: How many new Assembly constituencies were created for the Jammu region under the 2022 delimitation order for the UT of J&K?
faqs.e: One new Assembly constituency was created for the Kashmir region.

faqs.q: Which Parliamentary Constituency was carved out in the UT of J&K by combining the Anantnag area of Kashmir with the Rajouri and Poonch areas of Jammu?
Under the 2022 delimitation order for the UT of J&K, how many Assembly constituencies are reserved for the Scheduled Tribes?
faqs.e: Of these, 6 are in the Jammu region and 3 are in the Kashmir region; 7 Assembly constituencies are separately reserved for the Scheduled Castes.

faqs.q: The North Eastern Council was established through which Act of Parliament?
faqs.e: This Act repealed the earlier North Eastern Council Act, 1970, and came into force in 1972.

faqs.q: Which state became the eighth member state of the North Eastern Council in 2002?
Where is the Secretariat (headquarters) of the North Eastern Council located?
The North Eastern Council operates under the administrative control of which Ministry?

options.b: Ministry of Development of the North Eastern Region (DONER)

faqs.a: Ministry of Development of the North Eastern Region (DONER)

faqs.q: By virtue of the 2002 Amendment to the North Eastern Council Act, the Council was designated as:

options.c: the Regional Planning Body for the north eastern region
options.d: the apex disaster management authority for the region

faqs.a: the Regional Planning Body for the north eastern region

faqs.q: Since July 2018, who serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the North Eastern Council?
faqs.e: The Minister (in-charge) of the Ministry of DONER serves as the ex-officio Vice-Chairman of the Council.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the North Eastern Council:
(I) The Governors of the eight member states are members.
(II) Three members are nominated by the President of India.
(III) The President of India nominates the Chairman of the Council.
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: This reflects the original statutory scheme; since July 2018, however, the Union Home Minister has been designated ex-officio Chairman.

faqs.q: In 2003, the Ministry of DONER constituted which committee to suggest measures to operationalise the revised mandate of the North Eastern Council as a Regional Planning Body?
faqs.e: This Committee, headed by P.P. Shrivastav, submitted its report to the Government in 2004.

faqs.q: Who headed the North Eastern Council Revitalisation Committee that submitted its report in 2004?
